metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s. Beloved
units.rightText: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs. The Bride
rightNotes: 1:1 Most translators add subheadings for speaker identifications such as The Bride, The Groom, and The Friends based on the gender and number of the Hebrew words.

units.leftText: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than wine.
units.rightText: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.

units.leftText: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.
units.rightText: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.

units.leftText: Take me away with you. Let’s hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! Beloved They are right to love you.
units.rightText: Take me away with you— let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. The Friends We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. The Bride It is only right that they adore you.

units.leftText: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.
units.rightText: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.

units.leftText: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.
units.rightText: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.

units.leftText: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon; for why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of your companions? Lover
units.rightText: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions? The Friends

units.leftText: If you don’t know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
units.rightText: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds. The Bridegroom

units.leftText: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
units.rightText: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.

units.leftText: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels. Friends
units.rightText: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels. The Friends

units.leftText: We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver. Beloved
units.rightText: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver. The Bride

units.leftText: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
units.rightText: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

units.leftText: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.
units.rightText: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.

units.leftText: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi. Lover
units.rightText: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi. The Bridegroom

units.leftText: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves. Beloved
units.rightText: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves. The Bride
leftNotes: 1:15 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant. Lover
units.rightText: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed. The Bridegroom

units.leftText: The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.
units.rightText: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.

units.leftText: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys. Lover
units.rightText: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley. The Bridegroom
rightNotes: 2:1 Sharon Plain is a region in the coastal plain of Israel

units.leftText: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters. Beloved
units.rightText: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens. The Bride

units.leftText: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.
units.rightText: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

units.leftText: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
units.rightText: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.

units.leftText: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; for I am faint with love.
units.rightText: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.

units.leftText: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
units.rightText: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

units.leftText: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
units.rightText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

units.leftText: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
units.rightText: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.

units.leftText: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
units.rightText: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.

units.leftText: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
units.rightText: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.

units.leftText: For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
units.rightText: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.

units.leftText: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
units.rightText: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.

units.leftText: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.” Lover
units.rightText: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.” The Bridegroom

units.leftText: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
units.rightText: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely. The Friends

units.leftText: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom. Beloved
units.rightText: Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom. The Bride

units.leftText: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.
units.rightText: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

units.leftText: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
units.rightText: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.

units.leftText: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
units.rightText: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.

units.leftText: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
units.rightText: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.

units.leftText: The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
units.rightText: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”

units.leftText: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.
units.rightText: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.

units.leftText: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love, until it so desires.
units.rightText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right. Solomon Arrives on His Wedding Day

units.leftText: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?
units.rightText: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?

units.leftText: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
units.rightText: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
rightNotes: 3:7 That is, the couch on which servants carry a king

units.leftText: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.
units.rightText: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.

units.leftText: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.
units.rightText: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.

units.leftText: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
units.rightText: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.

units.leftText: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
units.rightText: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.

units.leftText: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.
units.rightText: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

units.leftText: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
units.rightText: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

units.leftText: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.
units.rightText: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.

units.leftText: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.
units.rightText: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.

units.leftText: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
units.rightText: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

units.leftText: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.
units.rightText: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.

units.leftText: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
units.rightText: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.

units.leftText: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
units.rightText: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.

units.leftText: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!
units.rightText: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.

units.leftText: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
units.rightText: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.

units.leftText: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
units.rightText: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.

units.leftText: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,
units.rightText: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,

units.leftText: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
units.rightText: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.

units.leftText: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon. Beloved
units.rightText: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon. The Bride
rightNotes: 4:15 Or flowing water or living water

units.leftText: Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.
units.rightText: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.

units.leftText: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved. Beloved
units.rightText: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. The Friends Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved. The Bride

units.leftText: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
units.rightText: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”

units.leftText: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
units.rightText: I have taken off my robe — must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?

units.leftText: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
units.rightText: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.

units.leftText: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
units.rightText: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.

units.leftText: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
units.rightText: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.

units.leftText: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
units.rightText: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.

units.leftText: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love. Friends
units.rightText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love. The Friends

units.leftText: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us? Beloved
units.rightText: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so? The Bride

units.leftText: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
units.rightText: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.

units.leftText: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
units.rightText: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.

units.leftText: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
units.rightText: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.

units.leftText: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
units.rightText: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.

units.leftText: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
units.rightText: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is polished ivory bedecked with sapphires.

units.leftText: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
units.rightText: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.

units.leftText: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you? Beloved
units.rightText: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you. The Bride

units.leftText: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
units.rightText: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.

units.leftText: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies. Lover
units.rightText: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies. The Bridegroom

units.leftText: You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.
units.rightText: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.

units.leftText: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.
units.rightText: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.

units.leftText: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing, of which every one has twins; not one is bereaved among them.
units.rightText: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

units.leftText: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
units.rightText: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

units.leftText: There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.
units.rightText: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number,

units.leftText: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed. The queens and the concubines saw her, and they praised her.
units.rightText: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises. The Friends

units.leftText: Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?
units.rightText: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession? The Bridegroom

units.leftText: I went down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.
units.rightText: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.

units.leftText: Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots. Friends
units.rightText: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people. The Friends
rightNotes: 6:12 Or among the chariots of Amminadab

units.leftText: Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
units.rightText: Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. The Bridegroom Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim ?
rightNotes: 6:13 Or the dance of the two camps

units.leftText: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
units.rightText: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.

units.leftText: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
units.rightText: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.

units.leftText: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
units.rightText: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

units.leftText: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
units.rightText: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.

units.leftText: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
units.rightText: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads; the king is captured in your tresses.

units.leftText: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!
units.rightText: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!

units.leftText: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
units.rightText: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.

units.leftText: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples.
units.rightText: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,

units.leftText: Your mouth is like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep. Beloved
units.rightText: and your mouth like the finest wine. The Bride May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.
rightNotes: 7:9 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew gliding gently over lips as we sleep

units.leftText: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.
units.rightText: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.

units.leftText: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s lodge in the villages.
units.rightText: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
rightNotes: 7:11 Or among the henna blossoms or in the villages

units.leftText: Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my love.
units.rightText: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom — there I will give you my love.

units.leftText: The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
units.rightText: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved.

units.leftText: Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no one would despise me.
units.rightText: O that you were to me like a brother who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.

units.leftText: I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.
units.rightText: I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.

units.leftText: His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.
units.rightText: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

units.leftText: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires. Friends
units.rightText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right. The Friends

units.leftText: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Beloved Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.
units.rightText: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? The Bride I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth.

units.leftText: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of the LORD.
units.rightText: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.
leftNotes: 8:6 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned. Brothers
units.rightText: Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, his offer would be utterly scorned. The Friends

units.leftText: We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?
units.rightText: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?

units.leftText: If she is a wall, we will build on her a turret of silver. If she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar. Beloved
units.rightText: If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver upon her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar. The Bride

units.leftText: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.
units.rightText: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace.

units.leftText: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
units.rightText: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. He leased it to the tenants. For its fruit, each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver.
leftNotes: 8:11 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 1000 shekels is about 10 kilograms or about 22 pounds.
rightNotes: 8:11 Hebrew a thousand of silver; that is, approximately 25.1 pounds or 11.4 kilograms of silver

units.leftText: My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon, two hundred for those who tend its fruit. Lover
units.rightText: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit. The Bridegroom

units.leftText: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice! Beloved
units.rightText: You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice. Let me hear it! The Bride

units.leftText: Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
units.rightText: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
